title: The Temple Carved From One Single Rock
description: Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved top-down out of a cliff, with no room for mistakes.

scenes.narration: This temple was not built. It was carved, from the top down, out of a single mountain of rock.
scenes.image_prompt: aerial view of Kailasa temple at Ellora carved out of a basalt cliff, deep rock-cut trench around it

scenes.narration: It's the 8th century, in Ellora, Maharashtra. The Rashtrakuta king Krishna the First has ordered something impossible.
scenes.image_prompt: ancient Indian king in royal attire overlooking a basalt cliff with architects, 8th century Deccan

scenes.narration: Workers start at the top of a basalt cliff and cut downward with chisels and hammers.
scenes.image_prompt: hundreds of ancient workers on top of a dark basalt cliff cutting down with iron chisels and hammers

scenes.narration: There is no room for mistakes. You can't add rock back.
scenes.image_prompt: close up of a sculptor carefully chiselling a detailed figure from dark rock, dust in sunlight

scenes.narration: An estimated two hundred thousand tonnes of stone is removed.
scenes.image_prompt: workers carrying away baskets of rock rubble from a huge rock-cut trench, rising temple shape inside

scenes.narration: Out of the cliff emerge towers, bridges, pillars and life-size elephants.
scenes.image_prompt: life-size carved stone elephants at the base of the Kailasa temple, towering carved shrine above

scenes.narration: The whole temple is shaped like Mount Kailash, the home of Shiva.
scenes.image_prompt: Kailasa temple at Ellora in golden light, multi-storey carved tower, dramatic sky

scenes.narration: Engineers still debate exactly how they did it. How do you think they managed? Tell me below.
scenes.image_prompt: wide view of Kailasa temple today with tiny tourists for scale, monsoon green hills
